news.headline: US military strikes Iranian rocket launchers near Strait of Hormuz — Crude WTI +2.30% to $85.32
news.what_happened: Over the weekend (Aug 30), the US military struck Iranian rocket launchers that were preparing to deploy mines into the Strait of Hormuz, escalating the 6-month-old US-Iran conflict. Oil prices surged at Asia open — WTI to $85.32 (+2.30%), Brent to $90.34 (+2.54%).
news.why_it_matters: The Strait of Hormuz carries ~25% of global crude trade. Any disruption risk spikes oil prices directly. India imports ~85% of its crude needs — higher crude raises import costs, pressures INR (though RBI FCNR inflows are partly offsetting), and widens the current account deficit. Sector-level impact is severe: airlines, paints, tyres, chemicals, logistics all face cost headwinds.

news.headline: Fed Chair Warsh hawkish at Jackson Hole — US 10Y yield surges to 4.72%, S&P -0.25%
news.what_happened: Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh delivered a hawkish speech at the Jackson Hole symposium on Friday (Aug 28), highlighting persistent inflation concerns and raising bets on a rate hike next month. US 10Y Treasury yield jumped 1.03% to 4.72%. S&P 500 fell 0.25%, Nasdaq -0.52%.
news.why_it_matters: Hawkish Fed signals higher US rates for longer → FII outflows from emerging markets including India. Adds pressure on Indian private banks, NBFCs, and real estate (rate-sensitive sectors). Nifty 50 FII ownership stocks like HDFCBANK, ICICIBANK, RELIANCE face selling pressure.

news.headline: China Manufacturing PMI August 49.8 — beats estimate (49.6) but second straight month of contraction
news.what_happened: China's NBS Manufacturing PMI came in at 49.8 for August (vs. 49.6 expected, 49.2 prior). Non-manufacturing PMI at 49.0. GDP growth Q2 2026 was 4.3%, below expectations. Factory activity improved but remains below the 50-point expansion threshold.
news.why_it_matters: China remains in mild contraction — demand for steel, aluminum, and other metals is weak. For Indian metal producers (TATASTEEL, JSWSTEEL, HINDALCO), the slight PMI improvement limits downside but does not trigger a bullish move. Neutral to marginally positive signal.

news.headline: RBI FCNR(B) swap window closes today Aug 31 — $52-60B forex inflows support INR
news.what_happened: RBI advanced the closure of its FCNR(B) foreign currency swap window to Aug 31 from the original Sept end date. Banks mobilised over $52 billion under the scheme, with total potential hitting $60-70B. The early closure came as a surprise after Governor Malhotra had signalled no early closure.
news.why_it_matters: Significant forex inflows into India are keeping USD/INR stable at 95.36 despite the crude surge. This is positive for India's macro — reduces immediate CAD pressure and prevents a sharp INR depreciation that would otherwise have occurred alongside crude's jump. Forex reserves are strengthening.

news.headline: MSCI India rebalancing effective today — 4 stocks added, 19 small-caps exit
news.what_happened: MSCI's semi-annual index rebalancing is effective August 31, 2026. Four stocks are being added to MSCI India indices, while 19 stocks exit the small-cap index. Passive funds tracking the index will rebalance at market close today.
news.why_it_matters: Forced selling in the 19 small-cap exits at or near market close could cause sharp late-session moves in those stocks. The 4 inclusions will see passive inflows. Adds to intraday volatility. Investors should avoid mid-session aggressive entries in unknown small-caps today.

picks.catalyst: Crude WTI +2.30% on US-Iran Strait of Hormuz military escalation
picks.logic: ONGC is India's largest upstream oil producer — every $1 rise in crude realization adds ~₹1,000-1,500 Cr to annual EBITDA. At +$1.92/bbl WTI overnight, this is a meaningful direct P&L uplift. With Brent at $90.34 (+2.54%), ONGC's Brent-linked realization moves in lock-step. Near-term geopolitical premium in crude is unlikely to reverse quickly given active Hormuz tensions. Strongest direct beneficiary in NSE.

BPCL holds significant crude inventory (weeks of supply) priced at previous lower levels. When crude rises sharply, the existing inventory is now worth more when refined and sold — a direct inventory gain. Q2FY27 inventory gains will be visible in quarterly results. Short-term bullish catalyst. Risk: if crude reverses, inventory gains reverse too. Government may also moderate retail fuel price hikes. Enter only on confirmation of hold above watch zone.

picks.catalyst: Crude WTI +2.30% → OMC inventory gain (same thesis as BPCL)
picks.logic: HPCL has historically been more volatile than BPCL on crude moves, offering higher beta exposure to the same inventory-gain theme. HPCL posted strong Q1 results (share rose 3% on results) and is entering this event from a position of improving refinery margins. Treat as secondary to ONGC — enter only if broader market sentiment is positive at open and crude holds above $84.
